title: Restart on save with nodemon
idea: nodemon runs your script with `node`, then watches your files and restarts the process every time you save a change.
points: Install it as a dev dependency, since only developers need it.
`nodemon src/index.js` replaces `node src/index.js` and watches the folder.
It watches `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs` and `.json` files by default, and skips `node_modules`.
A crashed app does not stop nodemon; it waits for your next save.

messages.label: node src/index.js
messages.note: `npm run dev` starts nodemon. It launches your entry file with Node and keeps watching.

messages.label: save a file
messages.note: You edit a route and save. nodemon sees a changed `.js` file.

messages.label: start again
messages.note: It starts a new process, so every module loads again.

messages.label: crash
messages.note: A typo crashes the app. nodemon stays alive and waits for a change.

messages.label: fix and save
messages.note: You fix the typo and save.

messages.label: start again
messages.note: The save triggers a restart. You never type `node` again.

code.title: Install and run
code.caption: `--save-dev` adds nodemon under `devDependencies`. Then you run the `dev` script.

code.title: Two scripts
code.caption: Keep both: `dev` for you, `start` for the server in production.

walk.text: `npm start` runs plain `node`: no watching, no restarts.
`npm run dev` runs nodemon. Custom script names need `npm run`.

pitfalls: Use `npm start`, which runs plain `node`, in production; nodemon is for development.
A restart starts a fresh process, so anything held in memory is lost.
nodemon ignores `.env` edits by default; type `rs` to restart by hand.
takeaway: Use nodemon while you develop; run plain `node` in production.
